key_insight: Scaling ego-centric video data helps world models, but not evenly: a 100x increase improves both agent behavior and object interactions, yet the gains are imbalanced. The paper shows that even 30,000 hours of video is not enough to fully teach robust, transferable world understanding.
problem_solved: This paper tackles the question of how far large-scale ego-centric human video can improve world models, especially for challenging out-of-distribution settings where standard simulator-based assumptions and opaque metrics can hide weaknesses.
method: Train/evaluate world-model learning with a massive ego-centric video dataset: 30,000 hours, 1,000+ scene types, and 14,000 contributors.
Directly measure agent fidelity and object-interaction fidelity instead of relying only on downstream proxy metrics.
Test on a challenging out-of-distribution benchmark to assess generalization under distribution shift.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows that more video data alone is not a complete solution for world modeling. It highlights the need for better evaluation targets and training strategies that specifically improve both agent behavior and physical interaction understanding.

paper_title: What 30,000 Hours of Ego-centric Video Does Not Teach
paper_authors: Jiahua Dong, Anurag Bagchi, Yash Jangir, Muhammad Zubair Irshad, Sergey Zakharov
